MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center

Patient: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
FKRP-related muscular dystrophy testing. Suspected congenital muscular dystrophy type 1C (MDC1C) or limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I (LGMD2I).

TEST PERFORMED
DNA sequencing screen of FKRP gene

METHODOLOGY
Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood. All coding exons and flanking intronic sequences of the FKRP gene (NM_024301.4) were amplified by PCR and analyzed by bidirectional Sanger sequencing. This test detects point mutations and small insertions/deletions in the coding regions and splice sites of FKRP.

RESULTS
FKRP gene: No pathogenic variants detected

All coding exons (1-4) and flanking intronic regions sequenced successfully with adequate coverage. No sequence variants identified.

INTERPRETATION
No mutations were detected in the FKRP gene. This result does not confirm a clinical diagnosis of FKRP-related muscular dystrophy. However, this negative result does not exclude the diagnosis as this test has limitations.

GENE INFORMATION
The FKRP gene encodes fukutin-related protein, a putative glycosyltransferase involved in the glycosylation of α-dystroglycan. Mutations in FKRP cause a spectrum of muscular dystrophies ranging from severe congenital muscular dystrophy type 1C (MDC1C) to milder limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I (LGMD2I).

TEST LIMITATIONS
• This test does not detect large deletions/duplications, deep intronic variants, or regulatory region variants
• Rare polymorphisms may interfere with primer binding and prevent amplification
• This test does not analyze other genes associated with muscular dystrophy
• Clinical sensitivity is approximately 85-90% for FKRP-related dystrophies

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
